interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative pathology reveals an adverse profile, including positive surgical margins, invasion of the seminal vesicles, lymphovascular invasion, and lymph node metastasis. The preoperative findings included a Gleason 3+4 with tertiary pattern 5 (ISUP grade group 2) and pathological stage pT3b. These findings are concerning. Countervailing factors are not documented in the provided reports. Nodal status is documented as positive for metastasis. The biopsy findings showed high-grade disease, with the second session identifying a Gleason 3+5 (ISUP grade group 4). The report states, "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 3+4 with tertiary pattern 5 (ISUP grade group 2), pathological stage pT3b. Extraprostatic extension was present; surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were invaded; lymphovascular invasion was present; lymph node metastasis was present." The presence of positive margins, seminal vesicle invasion, and nodal metastasis are significant adverse prognostic indicators. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, meaning biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its trajectory is crucial for revising the prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 30.32 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 24.26–36.38 months; its coverage has not been validated.
